aidan-lindisfarne-635.caption: 'Lindisfarne', a watercolour by Thomas Girtin of 1798, showing the ruins of the later medieval priory on Holy Island. The priory was built in the late 11th and 12th centuries on the site of Aidan's monastery; nothing of Aidan's buildings survives.
aidan-lindisfarne-635.author: Thomas Girtin (1775–1802)

alfred-athelney-878.caption: The monument to King Alfred at Athelney, put up in 1801 for the landowner John Slade on the site traditionally linked with Alfred's fortress and later abbey: a much later memorial, not a work of Alfred's time.
alfred-athelney-878.author: Simon Burchell

alfred-jewel.caption: The Alfred Jewel in the Ashmolean Museum, Oxford: rock crystal over a cloisonné enamel figure in a gold frame with the openwork inscription AELFRED MEC HEHT GEWYRCAN.
alfred-jewel.author: Mkooiman

aquae-sulis.file: Roman Baths and Abbey, IV, Bath, England-LCCN2002696370.jpg
aquae-sulis.caption: The Great Bath at Bath with the Abbey behind, a photochrom print of about 1890–1900. The pool is Roman, but the terraces, columns and statues around it are Victorian additions of the 1890s: a much later view.
aquae-sulis.author: Unknown photographer; photochrom print in the Library of Congress Photochrom Prints collection

augustine-canterbury-597.file: Luke St Augustine's Gospels Corpus Christi Cambridge MS 286.jpeg
augustine-canterbury-597.caption: St Luke, from the St Augustine Gospels (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 286), a 6th-century Italian gospel book long kept at Canterbury and traditionally, but not certainly, linked with Augustine's mission.
augustine-canterbury-597.author: Unknown Italian artist

battle-of-brunanburh-937.file: Alfred Pearseː The great battle of Brunanburh in 937 (Hutchinsons Story of the British Nation, 1922).jpg
battle-of-brunanburh-937.caption: 'The great battle of Brunanburh in 937', by Alfred Pearse, from Hutchinson's Story of the British Nation (1922): a much later imagining
battle-of-brunanburh-937.author: Alfred Pearse (1855–1933)

battle-of-hastings-1066.caption: Bayeux Tapestry, scene 57: King Harold is killed (embroidery made within a few years of the battle, probably in England in the 1070s)
battle-of-hastings-1066.author: Unknown embroiderers

battle-of-stamford-bridge-1066.caption: The Battle of Stamford Bridge, by Peter Nicolai Arbo (1870): a much later imagining
battle-of-stamford-bridge-1066.author: Peter Nicolai Arbo (1831–1892)

bede-historia-731.caption: A page (folio 3v) of the St Petersburg Bede, one of the earliest surviving copies of Bede's Ecclesiastical History, made in Northumbria within a few years of 731.
bede-historia-731.author: Unknown Northumbrian scribe

boudica-final-battle-60.file: Boadicea Haranguing the Britons (called Boudicca, or Boadicea) by John Opie.jpg
boudica-final-battle-60.caption: Boadicea haranguing the Britons: engraving by William Sharp after John Opie's history painting (published 1793). It is a much later imagining, not a record of the event or of how Boudica looked.
boudica-final-battle-60.author: William Sharp, after John Opie

caerleon-amphitheatre.file: Caerleon Roman Amphitheatre, From the north west - geograph.org.uk - 8232136.jpg
caerleon-amphitheatre.caption: The legionary amphitheatre at Caerleon from the north-west, built about AD 90 outside the fortress of Isca and excavated by the Wheelers in 1926–27.
caerleon-amphitheatre.author: Michael Garlick (Geograph)

camulodunum-destruction-60.file: Pictures of English History Plate IV - Boadicea and Her Army.jpg
camulodunum-destruction-60.caption: Boadicea and her army: colour print by Joseph Martin Kronheim from Pictures of English History (1868). It is a Victorian imagining of the revolt, not a depiction of Camulodunum or of any recorded scene.
camulodunum-destruction-60.author: Joseph Martin Kronheim

camulodunum-surrender-43.caption: Surviving remains of the Arch of Claudius in Rome, now in the Capitoline Museums, catalogued with its dedicatory inscription (CIL VI 920). The arch was completed in the early 50s and in its usual restoration claims that eleven British kings submitted to Claudius: a Roman monument to the event, not a view of Camulodunum.
camulodunum-surrender-43.author: Jenni Ahonen

carausius-usurpation-286.caption: A bronze antoninianus of Carausius, struck at his London mint in about 288–290, with his radiate bust (IMP CARAVSIVS P F AVG) and a lion for the legion IIII Flavia: one of the coins he issued as emperor in Britain.
carausius-usurpation-286.author: Classical Numismatic Group, Inc. (www.cngcoins.com)

columba-iona-563.caption: Iona Abbey in 2010. The church and cloister are later medieval Benedictine buildings, largely of the 13th to 15th centuries and restored in the 20th century; nothing of Columba's 6th-century monastery stands above ground.
columba-iona-563.author: Oliver-Bonjoch

constantine-iii-proclaimed-407.file: Impero d'occidente, costantino III, solido in oro (lione), 407-408.JPG
constantine-iii-proclaimed-407.caption: A gold solidus of Constantine III struck at Lyon in 407–408, soon after the army in Britain made him emperor and he crossed into Gaul.
constantine-iii-proclaimed-407.author: Sailko

constantine-proclaimed-york-306.file: Constantine the Great statue outside York Minster - DSC07907.JPG
constantine-proclaimed-york-306.caption: The bronze statue of Constantine by Philip Jackson outside the south door of York Minster, a modern work unveiled in 1998 near the site of the legionary fortress where he was proclaimed emperor in 306.
constantine-proclaimed-york-306.author: Rept0n1x (photograph); statue by Philip Jackson

coppergate-tenements.caption: The Coppergate Helmet, York Museums Trust. It was found at Coppergate in 1982, in building work that followed the main 1976–81 excavation. The helmet is Anglian, from the 8th century, so it is older than the 10th-century tenements, but it comes from the same site.
coppergate-tenements.author: York Museums Trust

cuerdale-hoard.file: Cuerdale Hoard in the British Museum.jpg
cuerdale-hoard.caption: Part of the Cuerdale hoard on display in the British Museum: coins, ingots and hack-silver from the lead chest buried by the Ribble around 905–910 and found in 1840.
cuerdale-hoard.author: Ethan Doyle White

cuthbert-community-chester-le-street-883.file: St Cuthbert's Church, Chester-le-Street by Graham Robson Geograph 5711685.jpg
cuthbert-community-chester-le-street-883.caption: The church of St Mary and St Cuthbert at Chester-le-Street, a modern photograph. The present building is mostly medieval, from the 13th century onwards, and is taken to stand on the site of the community's church of 883, inside the Roman fort.
cuthbert-community-chester-le-street-883.author: Graham Robson (Geograph)

cuthbert-community-durham-995.caption: A view of Durham Cathedral, a drawing of 1883 (Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum). The cathedral was begun in 1093, a century after the community settled here in 995, and houses Cuthbert's shrine.
cuthbert-community-durham-995.author: Unknown artist

cuthbert-community-leaves-lindisfarne-87.caption: Lindisfarne Priory, a watercolour by Thomas Girtin of 1798. The ruins are of the Benedictine priory built in the 12th century on the site of the monastery that Cuthbert's community left in 875, so this is a much later building.
cuthbert-community-leaves-lindisfarne-87.author: Thomas Girtin (1775–1802)

fishbourne-palace.caption: A dolphin mosaic floor in Fishbourne Roman Palace near Chichester. Some of the palace's floors belong to its first build in the 70s; others, including the famous cupid-on-a-dolphin floor, were relaid later, in the 2nd century.
fishbourne-palace.author: Charlesdrakew

hadrian-visit-britain-122.caption: A bronze as of Hadrian struck at Rome in about AD 119, with the seated figure of Britannia on the reverse, found on the Isle of Wight. It is a coin of the emperor, not a record of the visit, and was minted a few years before he came to Britain.
hadrian-visit-britain-122.author: Portable Antiquities Scheme (Isle of Wight Council)
hadrian-visit-britain-122.date: Coin c. AD 119; photograph recorded by the Portable Antiquities Scheme

hinton-st-mary-mosaic.file: Roundel mosaic christ hinton st mary british museum edit.JPG
hinton-st-mary-mosaic.caption: The central roundel of the Hinton St Mary mosaic, now in the British Museum: a clean-shaven male bust before a chi-rho, flanked by pomegranates, often read as Christ. A modern museum photograph of the 4th-century floor.
hinton-st-mary-mosaic.author: JMiall

hoxne-hoard.file: British Museum Hoxne Hoard Pepper Pots.JPG
hoxne-hoard.caption: Silver pepper pots from the Hoxne hoard, among them the 'Empress' pepper pot in the form of a woman's bust; a modern photograph of objects buried in the chest some time after 407/408, now in the British Museum.
hoxne-hoard.author: Andrew West (BabelStone)

inchtuthil-fortress.file: Den arkeologiske lämningen av fortet Inchtuthill med kant och upphöjt läge, floden Tay flyter (utanför bild) på tre sidor..jpg
inchtuthil-fortress.caption: The plateau above the River Tay at Inchtuthil, site of the unfinished legionary fortress of the 80s AD, photographed from the air in 2003; the Roman remains lie below the fields.
inchtuthil-fortress.author: Baron Delvine

lindisfarne-gospels.caption: Opening page of St Matthew's Gospel (folio 27r), Lindisfarne Gospels, early 8th century; British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV.
lindisfarne-gospels.author: Unknown Northumbrian scribe-artist (traditionally Eadfrith)

lindisfarne-raid-793.caption: Opening page of the Peterborough Chronicle (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle MS E, Bodleian Library MS Laud Misc. 636, written c. 1121), one of the manuscripts that records the raid under 793; this page is not the 793 entry
lindisfarne-raid-793.author: Scribes of Peterborough Abbey

londinium-destruction-60.caption: A surviving stretch of London's Roman city wall. The wall was built around AD 190–225, more than a century after Boudica's rebels burnt the unwalled town of about AD 60: a later monument of the same city.
londinium-destruction-60.author: John Winfield (via Geograph Britain and Ireland)

mildenhall-treasure.caption: The Great Dish from the Mildenhall treasure, with the mask of Oceanus at the centre and a Bacchic procession round the rim; a modern photograph of the 4th-century silver dish in the British Museum.
mildenhall-treasure.author: amandabhslater (Flickr)

mona-attack-60.file: Admiralty Chart No 1464 Menai Strait Wales, Published 1894.jpg
mona-attack-60.caption: Admiralty chart of the Menai Strait, the shallow channel between mainland Wales and Anglesey (Mona) that Suetonius Paulinus's troops crossed by boat and on horseback. Published 1894; Tacitus gives no landing place, so the exact crossing point is unknown.
mona-attack-60.author: Hydrographic Office of the Admiralty (UK Government)

repton-winter-camp-873.file: The Repton Stone, Derby Museum, Derby.jpg
repton-winter-camp-873.caption: The Repton Stone, part of an 8th-century carved cross shaft, now in Derby Museum. It was found in 1979 during the Biddles' excavations beside St Wystan's church, the site of the Viking camp of 873–4. The carving is about a century older than the camp.
repton-winter-camp-873.author: eamoncurry (Flickr)

rescript-of-honorius-410.caption: A gold solidus of the emperor Honorius found in Britain and recorded by the Portable Antiquities Scheme. The coin shows the emperor said to have written to the British cities in 410; it is not evidence for the letter itself.
rescript-of-honorius-410.author: Kurt Adams, Portable Antiquities Scheme

richborough-invasion-base-43.caption: The ruins at Richborough (Rutupiae), Kent, in 2004. The standing stone walls belong to the late 3rd-century Saxon Shore fort, built long after the Claudian invasion base whose ditches were excavated on the same site.
richborough-invasion-base-43.author: Val Vannet

river-battle-43.file: A Plan of the River Medway. with the Fortifications adjacent &c. (1725).jpg
river-battle-43.caption: A plan of the River Medway and its fortifications, 1725. Dio does not name the river of the AD 43 battle; the Medway is the traditional identification, so this shows the candidate river, not the battlefield.
river-battle-43.author: Unknown mapmaker

severus-death-york-211.file: Portrait of family of Septimius Severus - Altes Museum - Berlin - Germany 2017.jpg
severus-death-york-211.caption: The Severan Tondo, a painted wooden panel of about AD 200, probably from Egypt, showing Septimius Severus with Julia Domna and their sons Caracalla and Geta (Geta's face scratched out after his murder). It was painted about a decade before the family came to Britain; Antikensammlung, Berlin.
severus-death-york-211.author: José Luiz Bernardes Ribeiro (photograph); unknown Roman painter

silchester-ogham-stone.caption: The Roman town wall of Calleva Atrebatum at Silchester, inside which the ogham stone was found in a well in 1893. The stone itself, now in Reading Museum, is not shown.
silchester-ogham-stone.author: Simon Burchell

staffordshire-hoard.caption: Gold and silver fragments from a helmet in the Staffordshire Hoard, photographed after discovery for the Portable Antiquities Scheme.
staffordshire-hoard.author: Portable Antiquities Scheme

sutton-hoo-mound1.caption: The great gold belt buckle from the Mound 1 ship burial at Sutton Hoo, now in the British Museum; a modern photograph of one of the early 7th-century grave goods.
sutton-hoo-mound1.author: Rob Roy (RobRoy)

synod-of-whitby-664.file: Benjamin Brecknell Turner - Whitby Abbey, Yorkshire, North Transept - Google Art Project.jpg
synod-of-whitby-664.caption: The north transept of Whitby Abbey, photographed by Benjamin Brecknell Turner in the 1850s. The ruins are of the 13th-century abbey, built long after the synod on the headland where the earlier monastery stood.
synod-of-whitby-664.author: Benjamin Brecknell Turner (1815–1894)

tintagel-trading-site.file: Tintagel, King Arthur's Castle from valley, II, Cornwall, England-LCCN2002696619.jpg
tintagel-trading-site.caption: Tintagel headland from the valley, a photochrom print of about 1890–1900. The ruins are of the 13th-century castle, much later than the post-Roman settlement; the title 'King Arthur's Castle' reflects the later legend, not the evidence.
tintagel-trading-site.author: Unknown photographer; photochrom print in the Library of Congress Photochrom Prints collection

verulamium-destruction-60.caption: Remains of the Roman town wall of Verulamium, St Albans, with the cathedral in the distance. The wall dates from the 3rd century, long after the Boudican fire of about AD 60 that burnt the timber shops on Watling Street.
verulamium-destruction-60.author: Gary Houston

vindolanda-tablets.caption: Vindolanda tablet 291 (Tab. Vindol. II 291), Claudia Severa's birthday invitation to Sulpicia Lepidina, written in ink on a thin wooden leaf around AD 100; now in the British Museum.
vindolanda-tablets.author: Fæ

wearmouth-foundation-674.caption: St Peter's Church, Monkwearmouth. The west wall and porch, at the foot of the tower, survive from Benedict Biscop's church of 674; the upper tower is later Anglo-Saxon work and much of the rest of the church is medieval or later.
wearmouth-foundation-674.author: R J McNaughton (Geograph)

william-lands-pevensey-1066.caption: Bayeux Tapestry, scene 38: Duke William's fleet crosses the sea and comes to Pevensey (embroidery of the 1070s)
william-lands-pevensey-1066.author: Unknown embroiderers
